defs: to look at something to see if it is all right
to make sure something is good or correct
to take a look to find out how something is
exs: Please check on the baby.
Always check your answers before you hand in the test.
Mom will check if the cake is ready.

defs: to go up or into something
to move up or over something using hands and feet
to get into something by stepping up
exs: Be careful when you climb into the tub.
The monkey likes to climb the tall tree.
Climb up the ladder slowly.

defs: to breathe in quickly because you are surprised
to take a sudden short breath because of a shock
to suck in air quickly
exs: Everyone began to gasp when the lights went out.
I gasp every time the scary part of the movie starts.
You will gasp when you see the huge cake!

defs: to rest your body on something
rested flat on top of something
was stretched out on a surface
exs: Yesterday the dog lay on the sofa all day.
Last night, I lay on the grass and watched the stars.
The baby lay on a soft blanket.

defs: to make a long, low sound when you are unhappy or in pain
to make a sad sound because you are unhappy
to complain in a low, sad voice
exs: He began to moan when he saw all the homework.
The sick puppy began to moan softly.
Mom heard Carlos moan about the cold morning.

defs: looked at someone with an angry face
frowned because you were angry or upset
gave a cross, unhappy look
exs: Dad scowled when I broke the cup.
The boy scowled at his broken toy.
She scowled when her brother took her seat.

defs: the highest part of something
the highest place or point
the upper end of a hill or tower
exs: Don't fill the cup to the top.
Carlos climbed to the top of the hill.
Put the red book on top of the pile.

defs: not having or not doing something
not having someone or something with you
used when you do not do an action
exs: He left without saying goodbye.
I can't see without my glasses.
She walked home without an umbrella.

defs: a special way things are arranged; also something you tell someone to do
the way things come one after another
to tell someone what they must do
exs: Please say the numbers in order.
Line up in order from short to tall.
The captain gave an order to the robots.

defs: a small bag
a bag on a kangaroo for carrying its baby
a little bag for keeping small things
exs: The kangaroo keeps her baby in a pouch.
Mosh peeked out of the pouch.
She kept her coins in a small pouch.

defs: to make a loud, deep sound, or to laugh very loudly
to make a very loud, deep sound like a lion
to shout or laugh very loudly
exs: The class began to roar with laughter.
The lion began to roar at the zoo.
The crowd began to roar when the team scored.

defs: doing or giving something together with others
letting other people have a part of what you have
using something together with friends
exs: It is time for sharing, so tell us about your weekend.
Sharing your snacks makes friends happy.
Carlos likes sharing his toys with Mosh.

defs: the sound you make when you speak
what comes out of your mouth when you talk or sing
the sound a person makes when speaking
exs: She has a sweet voice.
Carlos heard a strange voice in the dark.
The singer has a beautiful voice.

defs: in a quiet way, without worry
in a relaxed way, not scared or angry
quietly and without getting upset
exs: She calmly walked out of the room.
Carlos spoke calmly to the frightened puppy.
The captain calmly told everyone to sit down.

defs: the leader of a ship, team or group
the person in charge of a plane, ship or team
the boss on a ship
exs: Our team captain is Tom.
The captain steered the ship through the storm.
Who will be captain of our soccer team?

defs: sad because things were not as good as you hoped
unhappy because you did not get what you wanted
a little sad about something that went wrong
exs: I was disappointed when the game was cancelled.
Carlos felt disappointed when it rained on picnic day.
She was disappointed with her low score.

defs: worried about something that will happen
feeling a little scared before something big
jumpy and worried inside
exs: I felt nervous on my first day of school.
She felt nervous before singing on stage.
The nervous boy bit his nails before the test.

defs: a person with an important job on a ship, or in the army or police
someone with a high job on a ship or in the army
a person in charge who gives orders
exs: The officer on the ship helped the captain.
The police officer helped us cross the street.
An officer showed the visitors around the ship.

defs: what a person in a play says and does
a role an actor plays in a show
a piece of something bigger
exs: I want the part of the captain in the play.
She has the funniest part in the school play.
Carlos learned his part by heart.

defs: to say that you will surely do something
to tell someone you will certainly do something
to give your word
exs: I promise to be on time.
I promise to feed Mosh every day.
Please promise you will not tell the secret.

defs: a break from class
the time between lessons when kids go out to play
a short school break for playing
exs: We play ball at recess.
Carlos played tag with his friends at recess.
The bell rang for recess.

defs: said something in an angry or mean way
spoke in a sharp, cross voice to someone
said words quickly in an unkind, grumpy way
exs: Mom snapped at us when we were too loud.
The tired teacher snapped at the noisy class.
"Leave me alone!" he snapped at his little sister.
